    What is at risk: PREMISE-124's UNCALIBRATED discipline, which is the register's only standing block on favourable self-produced numbers, and which PREMISE-124's own Applicable-to line binds to 15a/15b/15c/15d self-reporting. Also REVISE-253's pending amendment, which would take effect on unmeasured ground.
    Recommended action: Amend REVISE-253 with a pre-adoption gate, four clauses. (1) Before the three-state convention is adopted, compute the PARTITION FRACTION over the existing UNCALIBRATED population: for each item attempt to state an outcome scale and a worst-case bound on it, and record one of three outcomes — bound computed AND strictly narrower than the logical range / bound computed but trivial / no scale statable. (2) Fix the adoption threshold BEFORE running (1); below it, the amendment is withdrawn rather than weakened. (3) Entry to the new state must carry the COMPUTED BOUND in the entry, so an empty bound field is a schema violation and not a judgment call — this is the clause that answers Krosnick. (4) Items in the new state must receive a DIFFERENT subsequent action from UNCALIBRATED items, or the state is descriptive rather than action-bearing (Der Kiureghian & Ditlevsen's test). Consider also the alternative the logic literature actually recommends — a possibility/necessity or interval pair attached to the EXISTING two states — which adds expressiveness without adding a category to satisfice into.
    Urgency: Medium-High (the gate must be in place before adoption; it is not urgent otherwise, and the measurement is in-house and cheap)

  CORRELATION NOTE (PREMISE-120): both directions cite Manski's bounds programme, Ciucci/Dubois/Lawry 2014 and Graydon & Holloway 2017. DISPOSITION-566:
  Date: 2026-07-31
  Item: PRESUMPTION-592
  Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)

  15a result: SUPPORTED
  15a strength: Strong
  15b result: PARTIALLY-CHALLENGED

  Net assessment: The two directions AGREE on the category claim and disagree only about the remedy and the magnitude. 15a establishes it theoretically: termination is a liveness property, liveness is not confirmable from a finite prefix, artifact inspection is a finite observation. 15b does not contest this — its steelman concedes "the defect, if any, is in the verdict's label" and its first mitigation is to relabel PASS to name its evidence class. What 15b defeats is the item's implied remedy: the SRE position that black-box symptom monitoring is the right paging signal, the Two Generals result that no completion signal is reliable either, and the alerting-discipline objection that an unthresholded "still running" branch is unactionable. 15b also correctly notes the analogy to PREMISE-110's stuck-at fault is imperfect in the direction that matters — a fresh artifact is new evidence, not a frozen reading.

  Disposition: REVISE

  Reasoning: THIS WAS THE BATCH'S STRONGEST INCORPORATE CANDIDATE AND IT IS NOT BEING MINTED, for a reason found by the pre-check rather than by the searches. PREMISE-110 is ACTIVE, High confidence, and its Applicable-to line names "the scheduler watchdog" explicitly — so the watchdog is already governed. But PREMISE-110's prescribed safe form is "affirmative and perishable — the monitor must be actively fed on an independent timebase, so that cessation of activity is itself the alarm," and the watchdog SATISFIES that prescription: artifact recency is affirmative, perishable, and actively fed. It went false-green anyway. That is not an application of PREMISE-110; it is a defect IN PREMISE-110, whose remedy clause does not specify WHICH signal must be fed. Minting a new premise would leave the defective one standing and create two overlapping records for a reader to adjudicate. The correct output is therefore a narrow amendment to an ACTIVE premise, which is a REVISE. Urgency is Medium and not High because the observed instance is n=1 and the false-green RATE is unmeasured — entered UNCALIBRATED per PREMISE-124, and this disposition must not be read as evidence the rate is material.
  ON NOT SPLITTING: the magnitude question could have been routed separately to MONITOR. It is not, because a separate MONITOR entry would add a register entry without adding an action — the measurement is already named as this flag's validating test. Recorded explicitly because PRESUMPTION-577 / MONITOR-493 holds that consolidating findings may depress their salience, and a run that consolidates should say when and why. This run's consolidation rate on adverse findings is 1 of 4 (this item consolidated; 591, 600 and the systemic flag kept separate). That denominator is too small to establish symmetry and is recorded as UNCALIBRATED per PREMISE-124, not as compliance.

  If REVISE:
    What is at risk: PREMISE-110 as written, and every green signal in the fleet health report that its Applicable-to line covers. The watchdog is the only layer asserting fleet health, and its PASS is currently readable as a termination claim it cannot support.
    Recommended action: Amend PREMISE-110 with one clause and relabel one verdict. (1) AMENDMENT: the affirmative perishable signal must be the subject's TERMINAL STATE, not any of its outputs — an output is produced mid-execution and by construction cannot distinguish "finished" from "still going", because termination is a liveness property and no finite observation settles one. (2) RELABEL, near-zero cost and it discharges the whole documentation defect: change the watchdog's PASS to name its evidence ("artifacts present and fresh") so the termination inference is not silently available to readers. (3) DO NOT replace the artifact criterion with exit status — add terminal state as an ADDITIONAL field. Per SRE ch. 6 the symptom check should remain the paging signal, and per Two Generals the exit signal is a proxy too; a run that exits cleanly having produced nothing must still fail. (4) Introduce a "still running" state only WITH a duration threshold, or it is an unactionable branch.
    Urgency: Medium
    Validating test (in-house, cheap, decides the magnitude this flag leaves open): for the last N scheduled runs compare artifact write time against the scheduler's own terminal time — the distribution of that gap is how often and by how much PASS precedes termination; and separately, for runs that TERMINATED IN ERROR, check whether their artifacts were nonetheless fresh at check time. The second is the damaging case and is the false-green rate as 14b defined it. One instance is already on the record from the 07-30 EOD run (header 07-27, mtime 2026-07-28 15:39, a different but adjacent measurement).

Both readings are correct and compatible; that is one source doing work on two sides, not two sources agreeing, and no convergence is claimed from it.

The constructive half survives and is strengthened: the pre-check's FALSE-EXCLUSION RATE is unmeasured and unreported, which is the one thing the deduplication literature says must be measured, and it is measurable now at n=9 on the items the 07-29 pre-check removed. The destructive half falls: nothing licenses weakening the pre-check, and doing so on this evidence would restore the arrival rate into a zero-drain queue.     Recommended action: Three clauses, and clause (1) replaces the item's own test. (1) DO NOT run the cohort comparison the item specifies. Instead run the DIRECT test: take the 9 GOVERNED-CANDIDATE items the 07-29 pre-check removed and push them through 15a/15b/15c blind to the pre-check's verdict. Their conversion rate IS the false-exclusion cost, measured at n=9, needing no matched cohort and no cross-day comparability assumption. (2) ADOPT PRISMA-S-style reporting of the pre-check as a standing convention: count in, count removed, criterion applied, and measured false-exclusion rate, reported every cycle. ### Batch-level note from 15c (why six REVISE, and why that is itself a caution)

Six REVISE dispositions in a seven-item batch is far outside this pipeline's historical
rate and 15c is obliged to say so rather than present it as routine. Three readings, in
descending order of how well they are supported:

  (1) The batch is genuinely homogeneous. All seven items come from one 14b pass on one
      day's material, and 15b's flag shows five of them share a single root. A batch drawn
      from one root will disposition uniformly; that is expected, not suspicious.
  (2) The items are unusually decidable. Five of the seven meet literatures that are
      mature, quantitative and directly on point, and in four cases the supportive search
      returned empty against a populated field rather than against silence.
  (3) The dispositions may be correlated for the reason PRESUMPTION-631 names. 15a and 15b
      ran on one model in separate contexts, and 15c read both. If context separation does
      not deliver independence, this batch's unanimity is partly an artifact of the
      instrument, and 15c is the third reading of one opinion rather than a judge between
      two. 15c cannot rule this out from inside and does not claim to.

15c has NOT discounted the dispositions on reading (3); the challenges rest on external,
citable literature that is checkable independently of how it was retrieved, and REVISE
routes to human review rather than to automatic change. But (3) is the reason REVISE-262
is filed with High urgency: it is the only one of the six whose remedy would let a future
batch settle this question instead of restating it.

DISPOSITION-596:
  Date: 2026-08-04
  Item: PRESUMPTION-655
  Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)

  15a result: NO-SUPPORT-FOUND | 15a strength: None
  15b result: CHALLENGED | 15b strength: Strong

  Net assessment: The strongest convergence in the batch. 15a's finding is that the entire
  provenance field (W3C PROV-O) exists on the CONTRARY premise — a result is not
  interpretable independently of what produced it — so the presumption is the negation of a
  standard. 15b quantifies the consequence with Hsiao & Schneider (2021, QSS 2(4):1144):
  when a mark must be withdrawn, acknowledgement runs at 5.4%.

  Disposition: REVISE

  Reasoning: No support in a field whose founding assumption is the opposite, plus a
  measured propagation failure rate. The operational fact is decisive on its own: a
  retrieval method is known to have produced false affirmatives, and because no field
  records which method produced which mark, the affected set is not enumerable. That is
  unbounded exposure with a known cause and a cheap fix.

  If REVISE:
    What is at risk: every VERIFIED mark in the registers, of unknown count. Interlocks
      with REVISE-263 (ceasing to rely on a citation is not withdrawing it) — same defect,
      one register later.
    Recommended action: add a `method` and `date` field to every verification mark going
      forward, making the affected set enumerable by construction. For existing marks, the
      set cannot be recovered, so record that plainly rather than leaving the marks reading
      as sound: add a register-level note that marks predating the method field carry
      unknown provenance. Adopt VERIFICATION-WITHDRAWN as a third value.
    Urgency: High

  PROVENANCE:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b → 15a, 15b → 15c]
    Transform at this step: Net evaluation and disposition
    Current status: REVISION-FLAGGED

DISPOSITION-597:
  Date: 2026-08-04
  Item: PRESUMPTION-656
  Item type: PRESUMPTION (unstated — surfaced by inference)

  15a result: PARTIALLY-SUPPORTED | 15a strength: Weak
  15b result: CHALLENGED | 15b strength: Strong

  Net assessment: 15a found the precise form of the support and its precise limit:
  assume-guarantee reasoning (Cobleigh et al. 2003, TACAS) shows local correctness DOES
  compose — but only when the environment assumption is stated and separately discharged.
  Here the assumption is "escalation arrivals stay within service capacity," and it is
  undischarged. 15b found Bronson et al. (2021, HotOS '21) on metastable failure: once the
  queue tips, it does not recover when the escalation rate falls, and no local guard fires
  because every local actor is behaving correctly.

  Disposition: REVISE

  Reasoning: Both directions land on the same structure from opposite assignments — local
  correctness composes only under a discharged capacity assumption, and the metastable
  result says the failure is not self-clearing. The agent has already diagnosed its own
  mechanism; what is missing is a global-level guard, which by construction cannot be local.

  If REVISE:
    What is at risk: the review queue, and the honest-escalation norm itself, which is
      currently the starvation mechanism — a norm C2A2 should not weaken by accident.
    Recommended action: add a queue-level (not agent-level) invariant: measure arrival rate
      against service rate and alert on the ratio, not on any individual item's age. Add a
      retirement or aging rule so entries can leave the queue by a route other than service.
      Do NOT address this by asking agents to escalate less.
    Urgency: Medium-High

  PROVENANCE:
    Origin: 14b
    Chain: [14b → 15a, 15b → 15c]
    Transform at this step: Net evaluation and disposition
    Current status: REVISION-FLAGGED

  Net assessment: 15a found that the only theory under which "running" implies progressing
  is perfect failure detection, which requires full synchrony, known delay bounds and a
  crash-stop model — none of which hold here. Both directions independently reached Huang
  et al. (2017, "Gray Failure," HotOS '17): the system's own status monitor reports healthy
  while the component does nothing. 15b notes the interlock with PRESUMPTION-646 — a

  fail reassuringly together.

  Disposition: REVISE

  unchanged in turn count across three polls, one silent five months. That is not an

      — the intake basis whenever a session is listed but produces nothing.
    Recommended action: replace status polling with progress polling. Emit
      RUNNING-BUT-STALLED when turn count is unchanged across N polls, and set a maximum
      silent duration after which a session is declared dead rather than running. The

### ARRANGEMENT: what changed today, and what did not (partial answer to REVISE-262)

15a and 15b were executed as SEPARATE AGENT INSTANCES with disjoint contexts, dispatched by
a coordinating context that passed each only the eleven item statements. 15b was additionally
instructed not to read, list or grep `lit_search_results/for/`, which by then contained 15a's
completed output; its transcript shows no such access. This is a real improvement on
2026-08-03, where 15a, 15b and 15c ran sequentially in one context.

It is NOT independence in REVISE-262's sense, and the following residual is recorded rather
than glossed: both instances are the same model family and share pretraining and alignment,
which arXiv:2604.07650 identifies as the entanglement that survives architectural separation;
both were briefed by one coordinator, so both inherit its framing of each item; and 15b ran
after 15a rather than concurrently, so the barrier against contamination is instruction plus
transcript audit, not physical impossibility. Every "both directions independently reached X"
claim in today's dispositions — and there are four — inherits that residual.

Spot-check only. Of roughly 45 citations across the 22 result files, **3** were independently
verified at this pass. That is a small fraction and the other ~42 are recorded as UNVERIFIED,
not as sound. MONITOR-498 is open against exactly this gap and is not closed by this run.

    and manuscript level).
  · NOT VERIFIED — the specific figures. The contrast quoted in DISPOSITION-593 and REVISE-271,

    searches located the abstract and confirmed that both ICCs were estimated, but did not

    because the former is not negligible — and on 15a's finding that no source supports the
    item-attribution inference absent such a study. If the figures matter to a later decision,
    they must be read from the paper first.

backlog depth to demotivation in single-consumer review queues (677).

**15b (AGAINST) returns.** Strength of challenge Strong on all eight. Load-bearing
sources: Cristian 1991 and Mahmood & McCluskey 1988 (omission failure is a distinct class
from crash; a watchdog inside its own failure domain violates the one structural
requirement); Cemri et al. 2025 MAST (unaware-of-termination-conditions = 12.4% of
multi-agent-system failures); Skitka, Mosier & Burdick 1999/2000 (omission errors are the
class training does not fix); Tucker & Edmondson 2003 (93% first-order fixes; a successful
workaround removes the signal that would justify the durable fix); Dillon & Tinsley 2008
(recovered errors encode as successes); Yin et al. 2011 (14.8-24.4% of fixes are
themselves incorrect); Hu, Wang, Rubin & Pradel FSE 2025 (suppressions accumulate
monotonically, 50.8% stale-useless); Xu et al. OSDI '16 (latent configuration error -- a
limit that never fires is no evidence of compliance); Garcia-Molina & Salem 1987 and
Helland 2007 (partial state after interruption is the default, not the exception); Little
1961 plus EEMUA 191 / ANSI-ISA-18.2 numeric ceilings, and Sadowski et al. 2018 (84% of
tool-filed bugs never fixed; the remedy constrained the producer, not the consumer).
STEELMAN sections are in every file.
